questions.prompt: Which item is an example of a raised platform used when performing a task?
questions.correctAnswer: Step ladder
questions.explanation: A step ladder raises a person above ground level so a task can be reached safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks.

questions.prompt: Which raised platform is most suitable for reaching a high classroom notice board during display work?
questions.correctAnswer: Stable step stool
questions.explanation: A stable step stool is designed to support a person safely, while improvised supports can slip or collapse.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe raised platforms for simple school tasks.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of standing on a weak table to fix a wall chart?
options: Falling if the table breaks or tips
questions.correctAnswer: Falling if the table breaks or tips
questions.explanation: A weak or unstable surface may fail under weight and cause injury from a fall.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe risks associated with working on raised platforms.

questions.prompt: Before using a ladder, which check should a learner make first?
options: Confirm it is stable, dry, and undamaged
Carry tools in both hands while climbing
questions.correctAnswer: Confirm it is stable, dry, and undamaged
questions.explanation: Checking stability and condition reduces the chance of slipping, tipping, or equipment failure.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safe practices before working on raised platforms.

questions.prompt: A learner needs to collect materials from a shelf above head height. Which action is safest?
options: Ask for help and use a stable platform correctly
Jump repeatedly until the item falls
questions.correctAnswer: Ask for help and use a stable platform correctly
questions.explanation: Using the right platform with help keeps the learner balanced and protects people nearby.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety when working on raised platforms.

questions.prompt: Two learners are painting a school display stand from a low platform. Which behaviour shows safe teamwork?
options: One learner holds the platform steady while the other works carefully
Both learners push each other to finish faster
One learner climbs while holding open paint and scissors
Both learners stand on the same narrow edge
questions.correctAnswer: One learner holds the platform steady while the other works carefully
questions.explanation: Team support, steady footing, and controlled movement reduce the risk of falls and spills.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe teamwork practices when using raised platforms.

questions.prompt: Which situation has the highest fall risk during work on a raised platform?
options: A wet platform placed on uneven ground
A dry platform placed on a level floor
A ladder inspected by the teacher
A step stool used by one learner at a time
questions.correctAnswer: A wet platform placed on uneven ground
questions.explanation: Wet surfaces and uneven ground both reduce stability, so together they create a high fall risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse risks associated with working on raised platforms.

questions.prompt: A class is preparing rules for using raised platforms during project work. Which rule set is most complete?
options: Inspect the platform, place it on level ground, keep three-point contact, and avoid overreaching
Climb quickly, carry all tools at once, and work alone
Use any nearby object if it saves time
Stand on the top step and lean far to reach corners
questions.correctAnswer: Inspect the platform, place it on level ground, keep three-point contact, and avoid overreaching
questions.explanation: A good safety plan combines inspection, stable placement, safe climbing, and controlled reach.
questions.learningOutcome: Create safe rules for preventing accidents on raised platforms.

questions.prompt: Which substance is hazardous because it can easily catch fire?
questions.correctAnswer: Petrol
questions.explanation: Petrol is flammable, so it must be stored and handled away from heat and open flames.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify hazardous substances found in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which label would best warn that a liquid can burn skin or metal?
questions.correctAnswer: Corrosive
questions.explanation: A corrosive substance can damage living tissue or some materials, so it needs careful handling.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify hazardous substances found in the locality.

questions.prompt: Which group correctly classifies common hazardous substances?
questions.correctAnswer: Poisonous, flammable, and corrosive
questions.explanation: Hazardous substances can be grouped by the kind of harm they may cause.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify hazardous substances found in the locality.

questions.prompt: A learner finds an unlabelled bottle with a strong smell in the workshop. What should the learner do?
options: Report it to the teacher without opening or tasting it
Smell it closely to identify it
Pour it into the drain immediately
Mix it with water to reduce the smell
questions.correctAnswer: Report it to the teacher without opening or tasting it
questions.explanation: Unknown substances should be treated as hazardous until a responsible adult identifies and handles them safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Handle hazardous substances safely in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which practice shows safe handling of a small amount of corrosive cleaning liquid during supervised work?
options: Wear gloves, read instructions, and avoid splashing
Store it in a drinking bottle
Use bare hands to test its strength
Leave the container open near learners
questions.correctAnswer: Wear gloves, read instructions, and avoid splashing
questions.explanation: Protective equipment and instructions reduce direct contact and misuse of hazardous substances.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe and apply safe ways of handling hazardous substances.

questions.prompt: Why should hazardous substances be kept in clearly labelled containers?
options: Labels help users know the danger, instructions, and safe handling method
Labels allow learners to ignore the teacher
questions.correctAnswer: Labels help users know the danger, instructions, and safe handling method
questions.explanation: Clear labels guide safe use, storage, and emergency response.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the importance of instructions and labels on hazardous substances.

questions.prompt: Which storage choice creates the greatest danger in a school workshop?
options: Keeping flammable liquid beside a heat source
Keeping sand in a labelled bucket
Keeping clean cloths in a dry cupboard
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping flammable liquid beside a heat source
questions.explanation: Heat can ignite flammable substances, so they should be stored away from ignition sources.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse safe and unsafe storage of hazardous substances.

questions.prompt: A group is designing a hazardous-substance safety poster for the workshop. Which message is strongest?
options: Read labels, wear protection, keep containers closed, and report spills immediately
Open every bottle to check its smell before use
Store all liquids together regardless of labels
Use more substance than instructed to save time
questions.correctAnswer: Read labels, wear protection, keep containers closed, and report spills immediately
questions.explanation: The strongest message combines identification, personal protection, safe storage, and reporting.
questions.learningOutcome: Create safe handling messages for hazardous substances in the environment.

questions.prompt: What does self-exploration help a learner discover?
questions.correctAnswer: Talents, interests, strengths, and abilities
questions.explanation: Self-exploration helps a learner understand personal qualities that can guide growth and career choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of self-exploration in career development.

questions.prompt: Which activity can help nurture a learner's talent in designing practical items?
options: Joining a school innovation or technical club
Copying another learner's idea without learning
questions.correctAnswer: Joining a school innovation or technical club
questions.explanation: Clubs provide practice, feedback, teamwork, and opportunities to improve talents.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ways of nurturing talents and abilities for self-development.

questions.prompt: A learner is good at accurate drawing, measurement, and imagining 3D objects. Which pathway interest is most closely related?
questions.correctAnswer: Architecture or engineering design
questions.explanation: Spatial thinking, drawing, and measurement are useful in technical design careers.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate talents and abilities to career pathways.

questions.prompt: Which action is unethical when using a talent in a school project?
options: Taking credit for another learner's design
Practising a skill after school with permission
questions.correctAnswer: Taking credit for another learner's design
questions.explanation: Integrity requires acknowledging other people's ideas and work instead of claiming them as your own.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical and unethical practices related to the use of talents and abilities.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports a learner's choice of a technical career pathway?
options: Consistent interest, related ability, practice records, and feedback from mentors
Avoiding all information about the career
questions.correctAnswer: Consistent interest, related ability, practice records, and feedback from mentors
questions.explanation: A strong career choice is based on self-knowledge, evidence, and informed guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose a career based on talents and abilities for self-development.

questions.prompt: Which personal development plan best supports a learner who wants to become a product designer?
options: Practise sketching weekly, build small models, seek feedback, and record progress
Wait until Senior School before trying any design activity
Hide all sketches so nobody can comment
questions.correctAnswer: Practise sketching weekly, build small models, seek feedback, and record progress
questions.explanation: A useful plan includes regular practice, practical evidence, feedback, and reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple plan for nurturing talents toward a career pathway.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of oblique projection in technical drawing?
options: To show an object with front view and depth on one drawing
questions.correctAnswer: To show an object with front view and depth on one drawing
questions.explanation: Oblique projection represents a 3D object by showing the front face and receding depth lines.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the purpose of oblique projection in technical communication.

questions.prompt: In oblique projection, which face is usually drawn in its true shape?
questions.correctAnswer: Front face
questions.explanation: The front face is normally drawn true to size and shape, while depth is shown by receding lines.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic features of oblique projection.

questions.prompt: Which angle is commonly used for receding lines in an oblique sketch?
questions.correctAnswer: 45 degrees
questions.explanation: Many introductory oblique drawings use 45-degree receding lines to show depth clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe basic conventions used in oblique projection.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between cavalier and cabinet oblique drawing?
options: Cavalier uses full depth while cabinet uses half depth
Cabinet uses no front face while cavalier uses two titles
Cavalier is for bookkeeping while cabinet is for taxes
questions.correctAnswer: Cavalier uses full depth while cabinet uses half depth
questions.explanation: Cabinet oblique reduces depth to make the drawing look less distorted.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain types of oblique projection used in technical drawing.

questions.prompt: A rectangular block has a front face 60 mm wide and 40 mm high. In cabinet oblique, its 50 mm depth should be drawn as what length?
questions.correctAnswer: 25 mm
questions.explanation: Cabinet oblique commonly represents depth at half size, so 50 mm becomes 25 mm.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cabinet oblique principles when drawing simple objects.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is best for drawing a simple box in oblique projection?
options: Draw the front face, add receding depth lines, then join the back edges
Start with shading, erase all outlines, then add a title
Draw random depth lines before measuring the front face
Write the scale first and avoid measuring any edge
questions.correctAnswer: Draw the front face, add receding depth lines, then join the back edges
questions.explanation: Oblique drawing begins with the true front shape before depth is projected backward.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct simple objects using oblique projection steps.

questions.prompt: Why might a learner choose cabinet oblique instead of cavalier oblique for a long object?
options: It reduces depth distortion and gives a more realistic appearance
It removes the need for all measurements
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces depth distortion and gives a more realistic appearance
questions.explanation: Long full-depth receding lines can look exaggerated, so cabinet oblique shortens the depth.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse when to use different types of oblique projection.

questions.prompt: Which drawing error would make an oblique sketch difficult to interpret?
options: Using different receding angles for parallel depth edges
questions.correctAnswer: Using different receding angles for parallel depth edges
questions.explanation: Parallel depth edges should remain consistent so the shape communicates clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse common errors in oblique projection drawings.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to present a small desk organiser before making it from wood. Which drawing plan is best?
options: Prepare a neat cabinet oblique drawing with labels, scale, main dimensions, and title block
Draw only a front rectangle without depth or labels
Write the material cost without showing the shape
Trace an unrelated object from a magazine
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare a neat cabinet oblique drawing with labels, scale, main dimensions, and title block
questions.explanation: A complete technical drawing should communicate shape, size, and identity before production begins.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an oblique drawing plan for a simple product.

questions.prompt: In visual programming, what is a block?
options: A command piece that represents an instruction
questions.correctAnswer: A command piece that represents an instruction
questions.explanation: Visual programming uses blocks to build instructions without typing long code.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic features of a visual programming environment.

questions.prompt: Which block is most useful when the same instruction should run many times?
questions.correctAnswer: Repeat loop block
questions.explanation: A repeat loop makes a set of instructions run more than once.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the use of control blocks in visual programming.

questions.prompt: What does an event block such as 'when green flag clicked' usually do?
options: Starts a program or script when an action occurs
Calculates VAT automatically for every business
questions.correctAnswer: Starts a program or script when an action occurs
questions.explanation: Event blocks respond to user actions or system events and begin the connected instructions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain event-driven instructions in visual programming.

questions.prompt: A sprite should move 10 steps whenever the right arrow key is pressed. Which idea should the learner use?
options: An event block linked to a motion block
questions.correctAnswer: An event block linked to a motion block
questions.explanation: The event detects the key press and the motion block changes the sprite position.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply event and motion blocks to solve a simple programming task.

questions.prompt: A visual program should count points when a player collects an item. Which programming feature is most suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: Variable
questions.explanation: A variable can store and update a value such as score during a program.
questions.learningOutcome: Use variables to store values in visual programming.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a sprite to ask a safety question, receive a typed answer, and give feedback. Which block group is needed most?
questions.correctAnswer: Sensing and control blocks
questions.explanation: Sensing can receive input while control blocks can choose the next response based on the answer.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply visual programming blocks to create interactive feedback.

questions.prompt: Which mistake is most likely to stop a visual program from responding to a key press?
options: Forgetting the event block that listens for the key
Saving the file in a project folder
Testing the program after building it
questions.correctAnswer: Forgetting the event block that listens for the key
questions.explanation: Without the correct event, the program may have no trigger for the key-press action.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse errors in simple visual programming scripts.

questions.prompt: A program has start, repeat until score equals 5, move sprite, check collision, and add one point. What is the program mainly doing?
options: Creating a simple collection game with scoring
questions.correctAnswer: Creating a simple collection game with scoring
questions.explanation: Movement, collision checks, and score updates are typical parts of a basic collection game.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how visual programming instructions solve simple problems.

questions.prompt: A class wants to build a visual program that teaches safe handling of hazardous substances. Which design plan is strongest?
options: Use scenes, labelled choices, input checks, feedback messages, scoring, and a restart option
Use one sprite that moves randomly without instructions
Hide all buttons and remove feedback
Show only a blank background for five minutes
questions.correctAnswer: Use scenes, labelled choices, input checks, feedback messages, scoring, and a restart option
questions.explanation: An effective learning program guides the user, checks responses, and gives useful feedback.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a visual programming plan to solve a learning problem.

questions.prompt: Which material is obtained from trees and commonly used in making furniture?
questions.correctAnswer: Wood
questions.explanation: Wood is a natural material from trees and is widely used for furniture and simple products.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify wood as a material used in production.

questions.prompt: Which product is commonly made from wood in a school workshop?
questions.correctAnswer: Book rack
questions.explanation: A book rack can be made by measuring, cutting, joining, and finishing pieces of wood.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify products made from wood in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which property makes wood suitable for many classroom projects?
options: It can be shaped, joined, and finished with common tools
questions.correctAnswer: It can be shaped, joined, and finished with common tools
questions.explanation: Wood is workable, so learners can cut, shape, join, and finish it using appropriate tools.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe properties of wood used in production.

questions.prompt: Why is timber often seasoned before it is used in making products?
options: To reduce moisture and improve stability
To remove all need for measurement
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce moisture and improve stability
questions.explanation: Seasoning lowers moisture content, which helps reduce warping, shrinking, and cracking.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain preparation of wood before production.

questions.prompt: A learner needs a flat board for a small shelf. Which wood material is most suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: Plywood board
questions.explanation: Plywood is available as a flat sheet and is suitable for many simple board-based products.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable wood materials for simple products.

questions.prompt: Which action helps conserve wood during a class production task?
options: Mark parts carefully to reduce offcuts before cutting
Cut every piece larger than needed without planning
questions.correctAnswer: Mark parts carefully to reduce offcuts before cutting
questions.explanation: Careful marking and planning reduce waste and make better use of available wood.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible use of wood during production.

questions.prompt: Which comparison best explains a limitation of wood for outdoor products?
options: Wood is workable, but it can rot or be damaged by moisture if not protected
Wood is always waterproof and cannot burn
Wood is heavier than all metals and cannot be joined
Wood has no grain and cannot be finished
questions.correctAnswer: Wood is workable, but it can rot or be damaged by moisture if not protected
questions.explanation: Wood is useful but needs suitable treatment or finishing when exposed to weather.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse advantages and limitations of wood in production.

questions.prompt: Which product plan best uses wood responsibly for a school desk organiser?
options: Use measured pieces, reuse suitable offcuts, smooth rough edges, and apply a safe finish
Cut random pieces until one shape looks acceptable
Use wet timber and skip finishing
questions.correctAnswer: Use measured pieces, reuse suitable offcuts, smooth rough edges, and apply a safe finish
questions.explanation: A responsible plan considers material use, safety, quality, and final appearance.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple production plan using wood responsibly.

questions.prompt: Which item is a waste material from woodwork?
questions.correctAnswer: Sawdust
questions.explanation: Sawdust is produced when wood is cut or sanded and should be handled properly.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify waste materials produced during practical work.

questions.prompt: What is waste segregation?
options: Separating waste into suitable groups before disposal or reuse
Mixing all waste in one pile
questions.correctAnswer: Separating waste into suitable groups before disposal or reuse
questions.explanation: Segregation makes it easier to recycle, reuse, or dispose of waste safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safe ways of handling waste materials.

questions.prompt: Which group shows the three Rs of waste management?
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce, reuse, recycle
questions.explanation: The three Rs guide learners to prevent waste and recover useful materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain principles used in responsible waste management.

questions.prompt: A group has short plywood offcuts after making book racks. Which action is best?
options: Use suitable offcuts to make small labels or key holders
Throw all offcuts into a drain
Scatter them on the workshop floor
questions.correctAnswer: Use suitable offcuts to make small labels or key holders
questions.explanation: Reusing safe offcuts reduces waste and can produce useful small items.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply reuse practices when handling waste materials.

questions.prompt: Which personal protective equipment is most useful when sweeping dusty sawdust?
questions.correctAnswer: Dust mask
questions.explanation: A dust mask helps reduce inhalation of fine particles during dusty cleaning tasks.
questions.learningOutcome: Handle waste materials safely during workshop cleaning.

questions.prompt: Which waste-handling practice is most harmful to the school environment?
options: Keeping sharp offcuts in a safe container
questions.correctAnswer: Dumping mixed waste behind classrooms
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled dumping can cause injuries, pollution, pests, and blocked drainage.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse unsafe waste-handling practices in the environment.

questions.prompt: A school wants to reduce waste from project work. Which measure would have the greatest long-term effect?
options: Plan cutting lists, segregate waste, reuse offcuts, and keep records of material use
Buy more material than needed every time
Allow learners to leave waste on benches
questions.correctAnswer: Plan cutting lists, segregate waste, reuse offcuts, and keep records of material use
questions.explanation: Long-term waste reduction needs planning, sorting, reuse, and monitoring.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse strategies for reducing waste materials during production.

questions.prompt: Which plan best manages waste during a class woodwork project?
options: Assign bins for sawdust, reusable offcuts, sharp scraps, and general waste, then review disposal at the end
Wait until the room is full before cleaning
Mix all waste and let learners step over it
Put every waste item into the nearest classroom cupboard
questions.correctAnswer: Assign bins for sawdust, reusable offcuts, sharp scraps, and general waste, then review disposal at the end
questions.explanation: A complete waste plan identifies categories, collection points, safety needs, and final review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple safe waste-management plan for production work.

questions.prompt: Which tool is used to hold a workpiece firmly on a bench?
questions.correctAnswer: Bench vice
questions.explanation: A bench vice grips a workpiece so it remains steady during operations such as filing or sawing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify holding tools used in production tasks.

questions.prompt: Which tool is commonly used to hold two wooden pieces together while glue dries?
questions.correctAnswer: G-clamp
questions.explanation: A G-clamp applies pressure and keeps parts in position while glue sets.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify holding tools used for joining tasks.

questions.prompt: Why should a workpiece be held firmly before cutting or filing?
options: To prevent slipping and improve accuracy
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent slipping and improve accuracy
questions.explanation: Secure holding protects the learner and helps the tool follow the intended line.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of holding tools in production.

questions.prompt: Which practice protects a finished surface when clamping a wooden workpiece?
options: Place scrap wood pads between the clamp and the surface
Tighten the clamp directly until the wood dents deeply
Use oily hands to hold the workpiece instead
questions.correctAnswer: Place scrap wood pads between the clamp and the surface
questions.explanation: Packing pieces spread pressure and reduce clamp marks on finished surfaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safe use of holding tools on workpieces.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to file the end of a metal strip. Which holding method is most suitable?
options: Grip the strip in a bench vice with the working end exposed
Hold the strip in one hand while filing with the other
Place the strip loosely on a sloping desk
Ask a friend to hold it near the file teeth
questions.correctAnswer: Grip the strip in a bench vice with the working end exposed
questions.explanation: The vice keeps the strip steady and keeps hands away from the moving file.
questions.learningOutcome: Use holding tools safely for given production tasks.

questions.prompt: A learner is drilling a small wooden piece. Which action improves safety?
options: Clamp the piece securely before drilling
Hold the piece with fingertips near the bit
Drill without marking the hole position
questions.correctAnswer: Clamp the piece securely before drilling
questions.explanation: Clamping prevents spinning and keeps hands away from the drill bit.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply holding tools to improve safety and accuracy during production.

questions.prompt: Which holding-tool mistake is most likely to damage the workpiece?
options: Overtightening a clamp directly on soft wood
Using a clean bench vice correctly
Checking that the clamp is stable
Removing loose items from the bench
questions.correctAnswer: Overtightening a clamp directly on soft wood
questions.explanation: Too much pressure on soft wood can leave dents or crush the surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse correct and incorrect use of holding tools.

questions.prompt: A group is planning how to hold parts while assembling a wooden phone stand. Which plan is best?
options: Use a bench hook for sawing, clamps for gluing, pads to protect surfaces, and check alignment before tightening
Hold every part by hand during cutting and gluing
Use one clamp anywhere without checking the joint
Balance the parts on a stool until the glue dries
questions.correctAnswer: Use a bench hook for sawing, clamps for gluing, pads to protect surfaces, and check alignment before tightening
questions.explanation: A strong plan chooses holding methods for each operation and protects accuracy and surfaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan suitable holding methods for simple production work.

questions.prompt: Which tool is mainly used to drive nails into wood?
questions.correctAnswer: Hammer
questions.explanation: A hammer delivers controlled blows to drive nails into a workpiece.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify driving tools used in production tasks.

questions.prompt: Which tool is used to drive screws into wood?
questions.correctAnswer: Screwdriver
questions.explanation: A screwdriver fits the screw head and turns the screw into the material.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify driving tools used for fasteners.

questions.prompt: Why is a mallet preferred to a steel hammer when striking a wood chisel handle?
options: It reduces damage to the handle while giving controlled force
It makes the chisel sharper automatically
It replaces the need for safe holding
It turns the chisel into a measuring tool
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces damage to the handle while giving controlled force
questions.explanation: A wooden or rubber mallet spreads impact more gently than a steel hammer on many chisel handles.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe suitable uses of common driving tools.

questions.prompt: A screw head has a cross-shaped slot. Which screwdriver should the learner choose?
questions.correctAnswer: Phillips screwdriver
questions.explanation: A Phillips screwdriver fits a cross-shaped screw head and reduces slipping when used correctly.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable driving tools for different fasteners.

questions.prompt: Which practice is safest when using a hammer to drive a nail?
options: Hold the handle near the end, start with light taps, and keep fingers clear
Hold the nail close to the head until the final blow
Swing across another learner's working space
Use a loose hammer head to reduce effort
questions.correctAnswer: Hold the handle near the end, start with light taps, and keep fingers clear
questions.explanation: Controlled starting taps and clear fingers reduce injury and improve accuracy.
questions.learningOutcome: Use driving tools safely to perform given tasks.

questions.prompt: Which problem is most likely if a screwdriver tip is too small for the screw slot?
options: The tip may slip and damage the screw head
The screw will become a nail
questions.correctAnswer: The tip may slip and damage the screw head
questions.explanation: A poorly fitting screwdriver can strip the screw head and injure the user.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse tool selection errors when using driving tools.

questions.prompt: A learner bends several nails while joining two wood pieces. Which cause is most likely?
options: The hammer blows are not controlled or the nail is not started straight
The wood has been measured too accurately
The learner used a labelled waste bin
The workpiece was inspected by the teacher
questions.correctAnswer: The hammer blows are not controlled or the nail is not started straight
questions.explanation: Bent nails commonly result from poor alignment, excessive force, or unstable holding.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse faults that occur when using driving tools.

questions.prompt: Which plan best guides safe use of driving tools during assembly of a wooden frame?
options: Select matching fasteners and tools, secure the work, start gently, check alignment, and finish neatly
Use any available tool and strike as hard as possible
Skip marking and drive fasteners randomly
Let learners pass hammers while swinging them
questions.correctAnswer: Select matching fasteners and tools, secure the work, start gently, check alignment, and finish neatly
questions.explanation: Safe assembly requires proper tool selection, secure holding, controlled force, and quality checks.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan safe use of driving tools in a simple production task.

questions.prompt: What is the first step in a simple production project?
options: Identify the problem or need to be solved
Sell the product before making it
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the problem or need to be solved
questions.explanation: A project begins by understanding the need so the product can solve the right problem.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the problem to be solved through a production project.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner prepare a sketch before making a project item?
options: It communicates the shape, size, parts, and planned solution
It allows the learner to skip safety
It replaces the need for materials
questions.correctAnswer: It communicates the shape, size, parts, and planned solution
questions.explanation: A sketch helps the learner plan, discuss, improve, and make the product accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the importance of sketching during project planning.

questions.prompt: Which document lists the materials, quantities, and tools needed before production starts?
questions.correctAnswer: Project planning sheet
questions.explanation: A project planning sheet helps organise resources, time, tools, and responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe planning records used in production projects.

questions.prompt: A group wants to make a wall-mounted key holder for the staffroom. Which design requirement is most important?
options: It should hold keys securely and be fixed safely to the wall
It should use the maximum amount of waste
It should hide all labels from users
It should have sharp edges for decoration
questions.correctAnswer: It should hold keys securely and be fixed safely to the wall
questions.explanation: The design should solve the storage need while remaining safe and reliable.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply design requirements to a simple project problem.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best shows the production stage after a design has been approved?
options: Measure, mark out, cut, join, finish, and inspect
Paint, sell, guess, cut, and hide mistakes
Dispose, borrow, advertise, and begin measuring
Tax, insure, register, and ignore the product
questions.correctAnswer: Measure, mark out, cut, join, finish, and inspect
questions.explanation: Production follows an ordered process from preparation to making and checking the final item.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply production steps when making a simple item.

questions.prompt: A learner discovers a project part was cut 5 mm too short. What is the best response?
options: Review the drawing, decide whether to remake or adjust safely, and record the correction
Hide the short part inside the project without checking
Continue cutting all other parts randomly
questions.correctAnswer: Review the drawing, decide whether to remake or adjust safely, and record the correction
questions.explanation: Good project work uses evidence, correction, and records instead of hiding errors.
questions.learningOutcome: Solve simple production problems during a project.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps evaluate a finished project item?
options: Does it solve the identified problem safely, neatly, and within the planned resources?
Can it be hidden before anyone sees it?
Did it use every material even when unnecessary?
Was it made without any measurement?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it solve the identified problem safely, neatly, and within the planned resources?
questions.explanation: Evaluation checks function, safety, quality, appearance, cost, and resource use.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate a project item against the identified problem and planned criteria.

questions.prompt: Which project record would best show responsible teamwork?
options: A duty chart showing tasks, dates, materials used, and members' signatures
A blank page with no names or dates
A list of excuses for missing work
A secret notebook kept from the group
questions.correctAnswer: A duty chart showing tasks, dates, materials used, and members' signatures
questions.explanation: Clear records support accountability, fair participation, and follow-up during project work.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse project records for teamwork and accountability.

questions.prompt: A group must design an item to organise exercise books in a classroom. Which project brief is best?
options: Make a strong, safe, low-cost wooden book rack that fits a desk and holds at least ten exercise books
Make anything from any material without measuring
Make the largest item possible even if it blocks movement
Make a product with sharp edges because it looks modern
questions.correctAnswer: Make a strong, safe, low-cost wooden book rack that fits a desk and holds at least ten exercise books
questions.explanation: A good brief states the product, user need, safety, cost, size, and performance requirement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a clear project brief for a simple production item.

questions.prompt: Which final presentation best shows a completed production project?
options: Display the item with sketches, material list, cost record, safety notes, and evaluation comments
Show only the item and refuse to explain how it was made
Display loose waste without the product
Present a business poster for a different product
questions.correctAnswer: Display the item with sketches, material list, cost record, safety notes, and evaluation comments
questions.explanation: A complete presentation shows both the finished product and the evidence of planning, making, and review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a project presentation showing process and outcome evidence.

questions.prompt: Which institution in Kenya mainly accepts deposits and gives loans to customers?
questions.correctAnswer: Commercial bank
questions.explanation: Commercial banks provide financial services such as deposits, withdrawals, payments, and loans.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial institutions available in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which group contains only financial institutions found in Kenya?
options: Banks, SACCOs, insurance companies, and microfinance institutions
questions.correctAnswer: Banks, SACCOs, insurance companies, and microfinance institutions
questions.explanation: These institutions provide money-related services to individuals and businesses.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify financial institutions in Kenya.

questions.prompt: What service does an insurance company mainly provide to a business?
options: Protection against specified risks in exchange for premiums
Storing hazardous substances in open bottles
questions.correctAnswer: Protection against specified risks in exchange for premiums
questions.explanation: Insurance helps a business manage losses from covered risks such as fire, theft, or accidents.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse services offered by financial institutions in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A youth group wants to save monthly contributions and later borrow for a poultry project. Which institution is most suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: SACCO
questions.explanation: A SACCO supports members through savings and credit based on agreed rules.
questions.learningOutcome: Utilise financial services for entrepreneurial development.

questions.prompt: Which factor should a small business compare before taking a loan from a financial institution?
options: Interest rate, repayment period, fees, and ability to repay
Colour of the office walls only
Number of posters on the door
Distance from the nearest football field only
questions.correctAnswer: Interest rate, repayment period, fees, and ability to repay
questions.explanation: A responsible borrower checks the real cost of credit and whether business income can support repayment.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse financial services for entrepreneurial decision making.

questions.prompt: A learner is advising a class business project on financial services. Which plan is most responsible?
options: Open a group savings record, deposit income safely, insure valuable equipment if needed, and borrow only with a repayment plan
Borrow the largest amount available without checking income
Keep all cash loosely in a school bag
Hide sales records from group members
questions.correctAnswer: Open a group savings record, deposit income safely, insure valuable equipment if needed, and borrow only with a repayment plan
questions.explanation: Responsible financial management combines saving, record keeping, risk protection, and careful borrowing.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a responsible plan for using financial services in entrepreneurship.

questions.prompt: Why does the government get involved in business activities?
options: To protect consumers, collect revenue, and promote fair trade
To remove the need for records
questions.correctAnswer: To protect consumers, collect revenue, and promote fair trade
questions.explanation: Government involvement supports order, safety, fairness, revenue collection, and public welfare.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for government involvement in business.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of government regulation of business?
options: Licensing a shop before it operates
questions.correctAnswer: Licensing a shop before it operates
questions.explanation: Licensing is a way for government to allow and monitor business activities under set rules.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of government involvement in business.

questions.prompt: Which type of tax is commonly charged on many goods and services bought in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Value Added Tax
questions.explanation: Value Added Tax, often called VAT, is charged on many taxable goods and services.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore types of taxes in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A small motor-vehicle parts business needs official licensing information online. Which service channel is most suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: A relevant Kenyan e-Government platform
questions.explanation: E-Government platforms provide digital access to services such as registration, licensing, and official information.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse e-Government services in business.

questions.prompt: Which business behaviour best shows compliance with government regulations?
options: Registering the business, keeping records, paying due taxes, and following safety rules
Selling expired goods with changed labels
Operating without a licence to avoid fees
Dumping waste in a public drain at night
questions.correctAnswer: Registering the business, keeping records, paying due taxes, and following safety rules
questions.explanation: Compliance means following legal requirements and operating responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the need to comply with government regulations in business.

questions.prompt: A learner studies a case where a business avoids taxes but uses public roads, security, and markets. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: Avoiding taxes is unfair because public services need revenue and shared responsibility
Avoiding taxes improves fairness for all citizens
Taxes are only for businesses that sell wood
Public services do not need funding
questions.correctAnswer: Avoiding taxes is unfair because public services need revenue and shared responsibility
questions.explanation: Taxes help fund public services, so compliance supports social responsibility and fairness.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate ethical reasons for complying with government business regulations.

questions.prompt: What is a business plan?
options: A written guide showing how a business will operate and achieve its goals
A drawing of a raised platform only
questions.correctAnswer: A written guide showing how a business will operate and achieve its goals
questions.explanation: A business plan describes the idea, customers, operations, marketing, and finances of a business.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of a business plan in entrepreneurship.

questions.prompt: Which section of a business plan describes target customers and competitors?
questions.correctAnswer: Market and competitor analysis
questions.explanation: Market and competitor analysis explains who may buy the product and how other sellers affect the business.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe components of a business plan in financial management.

questions.prompt: A group wants to sell wooden phone stands at a school exhibition. Which detail belongs in the financial projection section?
options: Expected sales, costs, profit, and cash needs
Only the colour of the poster
Types of hazardous substances in the store
questions.correctAnswer: Expected sales, costs, profit, and cash needs
questions.explanation: Financial projections estimate money coming in, money going out, and expected results.
questions.learningOutcome: Fill in financial information in a business plan template.

questions.prompt: A business plan says the product will be 'useful for everyone' but gives no customer details. What improvement is needed?
options: Define the target customers and their needs more clearly
questions.correctAnswer: Define the target customers and their needs more clearly
questions.explanation: A useful plan identifies who the customers are and why they would buy the product.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply business plan components to a given business project.

questions.prompt: Which weakness would make a business plan unreliable?
options: The expected profit is estimated without listing costs or selling price
The plan names the product clearly
The plan includes a marketing method
questions.correctAnswer: The expected profit is estimated without listing costs or selling price
questions.explanation: Profit estimates need evidence from selling price, expected sales, and costs.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse components of a business plan for completeness.

questions.prompt: A class enterprise will make 30 recycled-paper notebooks. Which business plan summary is strongest?
options: State the product, target buyers, competitors, price, production costs, marketing method, roles, and expected profit
Write only the product name and start selling immediately
List tools but ignore customers, price, and costs
Copy another group's plan without checking whether it fits
questions.correctAnswer: State the product, target buyers, competitors, price, production costs, marketing method, roles, and expected profit
questions.explanation: A strong plan connects the business idea, market, operations, marketing, and finances.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a complete business plan outline for a given business project.
